data.name: Diamondbacks Activate Nelson, Designate Law for Assignment
data.hook: Ryne Nelson is back in the Arizona Diamondbacks bullpen after months sidelined by an elbow strain, bringing fresh arms to a team chasing the playoffs.
data.summary: The Diamondbacks activated right-hander Ryne Nelson, 28, from the 60-day injured list on Wednesday and designated reliever Derek Law for assignment to make room. Nelson returns with a 4.97 ERA from earlier this season and will pitch out of the bullpen during the stretch run, while Law, who posted a sharp 1.00 ERA in nine innings, now heads to waivers. Fans cheered the pitching boost but vented frustration over first baseman Pavin Smith's ongoing starts despite his .151 average, one homer, and seven RBIs in 86 at-bats, sparking questions about late-season roster choices.

data.name: Diamondbacks Start Struggling Pavin Smith at First in Key Marlins Game
data.hook: With the playoffs in sight, the Arizona Diamondbacks posted their lineup featuring Pavin Smith back at first base—and fans weren't holding back their frustration.
data.summary: The team shared the September 16 lineup against the Miami Marlins, putting Smith (.151 average, one homer in 86 at-bats) at first alongside 'Keep fighting,' while reinstating pitcher Ryne Nelson from injury and designating reliever Derek Law for assignment. At 80-72 and 2.5 games from the wild-card spot, supporters questioned starting the slumping Smith over prospects like Jordan Lawlar in this must-win stretch. GM Mike Hazen remains confident in playoff odds but wants more early scoring as roster choices spark tension with fans.

data.name: Corbin Carroll's Walk-Off Homer Lifts Diamondbacks Over Marlins
data.hook: Down 7-4 in the eighth, the Diamondbacks clawed back, and Corbin Carroll sealed it with a massive 423-foot blast to right field in the ninth.
data.summary: Corbin Carroll crushed a two-run homer in the bottom of the ninth at Chase Field, giving Arizona an 8-7 win over Miami after trailing 7-4 entering the eighth. Jordan Lawlar's two-run shot in the eighth set the stage, and Carroll's 21st homer of the year came right after a sacrifice bunt from Geraldo Perdomo. The victory was Arizona's MLB-leading 45th comeback and ninth walk-off, keeping them 2½ games behind San Diego for the NL wild-card spot with 11 games left.

data.name: Baseball America Releases 2026 MLB Farm System Grades
data.hook: The Milwaukee Brewers and St. Louis Cardinals topped the NL Central with A and A+ marks, while the Giants earned league-wide praise for their young stars.
data.summary: Baseball America graded each MLB organization's farm system based on prospect performances, graduations, breakouts, and trades during the 2026 season. Standouts included the Giants and Cardinals with A+ grades thanks to talents like Josuar Gonzalez and smart deadline moves, while the Cubs landed a C after trading top prospects but saw breakouts from Josiah Hartshorn and Owen Ayers. Other notables were the Rays at A, Yankees at C-, and Reds at D, reflecting a year of building depth or facing natural thinning.

data.name: Drew Gilbert's Pinch-Hit Homer Lifts Giants Past Cardinals in 10 Innings
data.hook: With the game knotted in the 10th, Drew Gilbert stepped up as a pinch hitter and crushed a 415-foot two-run homer to center, sending Giants fans into cheers.
data.summary: The San Francisco Giants edged the St. Louis Cardinals 6-5 in a 10-inning thriller at Busch Stadium, thanks to Gilbert's clutch blast off Riley O’Brien that scored automatic runner Grant McCray for a 6-4 lead.

data.name: Diamondbacks Slot Newcomer Sánchez in Lineup vs. Marlins
data.hook: Jesús Sánchez steps up to the plate in his Arizona debut, slotted seventh as DH while Pavin Smith holds down first base in a critical wild-card push.
data.summary: The Diamondbacks, sitting 80-71 and 2½ games from the NL wild-card spot, announced their lineup for Tuesday's home game against the Marlins with Michael Soroka starting.

data.name: Seahawks Slight Favorites Over Cardinals Despite ESPN Model Edge
data.hook: Both teams sit at 1-0 heading into their NFC West clash, but an ESPN analytics model picks Arizona to upset Seattle, stirring up fan rivalries ahead of Sunday's game.
data.summary: The Seahawks travel to Glendale for a 1:25 p.m. MST kickoff on FOX, with Drew Lock starting in place of the injured Sam Darnold. While betting lines favor Seattle by 3.5 to 4.5 points, ESPN's predictor gives the Cardinals a 53.7% win chance over the Seahawks' 45.9%. Fans are fired up—Seahawks backers embrace the underdog vibe they've thrived on historically with nine straight wins over Arizona, while Cardinals supporters eye a home upset like their 2020 victory.

data.name: Dodgers Poised to Clinch 13th NL West Title Against Reds
data.hook: The Dodgers stepped up in Cincinnati with a chance to lock up their 13th NL West crown in 14 years. A win or Padres stumble would do it, and fans could feel the buzz building.
data.summary: Los Angeles posted their lineup early, featuring Tommy Edman leading off, Mookie Betts at shortstop, Freddie Freeman at first, and Blake Snell starting on the mound for 'Snellzilla day.'

data.name: Seahawks Slight Underdogs vs Cardinals in Week 2 Clash
data.hook: With Sam Darnold sidelined by a glute injury, Drew Lock steps up for the Seahawks as ESPN analytics tilts slightly toward the Cardinals at home.
data.summary: Both teams sit at 1-0 after Week 1 wins, but the Seahawks now face a 53.7% win chance for Arizona per ESPN, flipping early betting lines from double-digit favorites to 3.5-point road favorites. Seahawks fans embrace the underdog mentality, while Cardinals backers eye a home upset after their strong road victory over the Chargers. Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Lock starts Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX, fueling back-and-forth excitement in the rivalry.

data.name: Cardinals Place Rookie Safety Kitan Crawford on IR with Ankle Sprain
data.hook: Kitan Crawford, the Cardinals' seventh-round pick, was carted off after a special teams play in their Week 1 win, leaving fans holding their breath.
data.summary: The Arizona Cardinals moved safety Kitan Crawford to injured reserve with a mid-ankle sprain from Sunday's victory over the Chargers. The injury isn't season-ending, and he's designated to return after at least four weeks, easing early worries. To address secondary depth issues—especially with safety Dadrion Taylor-Demerson sidelined by a rib injury—the team promoted cornerback Kalen King, released wide receiver Ihmir Smith-Marsette from the practice squad, and added safety Jerrick Reed II and cornerback Art Green.
